transcript.text: microwve plate wont go round anymore, food hot on one side cold on other. still heats tho

It is still heating, so this sounds separate from the main heating system. Uneven heating is expected when the turntable does not rotate. Most often it is simply the plate not sitting on its centre drive, a dirty/dislodged roller ring, or food debris stopping it. If those are all sound, the likely faults are the small centre drive coupler or the turntable motor. 1. Switch it off and unplug it. Lift out the glass plate.
2. Check the roller ring underneath: it should sit flat, its little wheels should turn freely, and there should be no hardened food or debris beneath it.
3. Check the small plastic drive in the centre. It should not be cracked, split or loose. Refit the plate so its underside grooves engage with it, and make sure a large dish is not rubbing the cavity sides. If anything was out of place or dirty, clean/reseat it and try a cup of water for a short run. If it still will not turn, tell me whether you can hear a faint motor hum/attempt to turn while the plate stays still, or whether there is no movement or sound at all. That separates a worn centre coupler from a turntable motor fault.

ok did it. roller ring is in and the wheels spin fine, nothing stuck under it. the little 3 pronged plastic bit in the middle has a crack and the hole looks rounded. with a cup of water it just wobbles and doesnt really turn, and theres a faint grinding/clicking from the centre. the metal bit under it moves a bit. i did drop the plate in the sink last week tho

The cracked, rounded three-pronged centre drive is very likely the fault. It is no longer gripping the drive beneath it properly, which explains the wobble, clicking/grinding and the plate not turning. The dropped plate may have damaged or worsened that plastic coupler. The likely repair is the turntable coupler, rather than the roller ring or the main heating parts. Do not open the microwave casing: this item is normally dealt with from inside the cavity only, with the appliance unplugged. The small amount of movement from the metal drive beneath, plus the centre noise, makes the turntable motor less likely at present. If a correctly fitted replacement coupler still slips or does not turn, then the turntable motor/gearbox would be the next suspect. Until repaired, it will still heat, but food will heat unevenly; pause and turn food manually if you need to use it.

candidates: Turntable tray not seated correctly, obstructed, or roller ring dirty/damaged (high)
Turntable drive coupler worn or split (medium)

plan: The fault they reported is: "turntable plate will not rotate; food heats unevenly". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
